newsitem.title: USA: Price talk portends well for Norfolk Southern deal.
newsitem.headline: Price talk portends well for Norfolk Southern deal.

text.p: Three days of solid price talk for the $3.0 billion Norfolk Southern Corp mutli-tranche debt issue should ensure a strong pricing and possible upsizing of the deal, dealers said.
Other dealers said a reach for yield will benefit Ba1/BB-plus rated Owens-Illinois Inc's $300 million issue.

Back in railroads, price talk of 45 basis points over the curve in five years, 70 basis points over in 10 years, 90 basis points over in 30 years and 45 basis points over for a 40-year bond with a seven year put option has held steady since first crossing desks on Friday, one manager said.

Elsewhere, junk-rated Owens-Illinois's $300 million seven-year issue, accompanied by $300 million 10-year notes, is already several times oversubscribed at aggressive levels, dealers said. The positive credit story and recent increased liquidity for crossover names has made the issue a darling of the day, one syndicate source said.
Price talk calls for spreads of 125 basis points over the curve in seven years and 140 to 150 over in 10 years.
Toledo, Ohio-based Owens-Illinois will use the proceeds from the offering and the sale of 14.75 million shares of common stock to refinance higher coupon debt.

Other "high-yield" offerings of Tuesday include Amphenol Corp's $240 million 10-year senior subordinated notes via co-managers Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette and Lehman Brothers. The deal, rated Ba1/BB-plus, could garner a yield through 10 percent, one dealer said.

The notes are part of a recapitalization plan prompted by the proposed merger of Amphenol with a Kohlberg, Kravis Roberts & Co unit. Amphenol shareholders will consider the merger at the annual meeting Wednesday, the company said.
Amphenol, based in Wallingford, Conn., is the world's second largest producer of coaxial cable. It also manufactures and markets flat ribbon cable, fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems.
